los.text: Identify the mons pubis, parts of the female external genitalia, vestibule, urethral orifice and vaginal orifice
los.html:
PartDescription
Mons pubisFat pad over the pubic symphysis
Labia majoraFatty, hair-bearing folds (homologue of the scrotum); round ligament ends here
Labia minoraHairless folds; in front they form the prepuce and frenulum of the clitoris
ClitorisGlans, body, crura (erectile)
VestibuleSpace between the labia minora, containing the openings below
External urethral orificeIn front, ~2–3 cm behind the clitoris
Vaginal orificeBehind the urethral opening; hymen
Greater vestibular (Bartholin's) glandsOpen posterolaterally (~5 and 7 o'clock): cysts and abscesses
Paraurethral (Skene's) glandsBeside the urethral meatus
Perineal bodyFibromuscular node between vagina and anus (episiotomy and tears).
SupplyPudendal (and external pudendal) vessels; ilioinguinal and genitofemoral nerves in front, pudendal behind; lymph to superficial inguinal nodes.

los.text: Identify the major viscera of the female pelvis
los.html:
Front to back
  • Bladder (behind the pubic symphysis) and urethra
  • → uterus (anteverted and anteflexed over the bladder) with tubes and ovaries
  • → vagina
  • → rectum and anal canal.
AboveLoops of ileum and sigmoid colon.
Ovarieson the side wall in the ovarian fossa, near the ureter and internal iliac vessels.
PouchesShallow vesicouterine pouch in front; deep rectouterine pouch (Douglas) behind, next to the posterior fornix.
UretersPass under the uterine arteries beside the cervix.

los.text: Describe the parts of the ovary, uterus and uterine tubes, and their anatomical relationships and function
los.html:
OrganPartsRelationsFunction
OvaryCortex (follicles), medulla (vessels); covered by surface epithelium, not peritoneum
  • Ovarian fossa
  • Obturator nerve lateral (pain referred to medial thigh)
  • Attached by the suspensory ligament (ovarian vessels), ligament of ovary and mesovarium
Oocytes, oestrogen, progesterone
Uterine tube (~10 cm)Infundibulum (fimbriae), ampulla (fertilisation, most ectopics), isthmus, intramural partUpper border of the broad ligament (mesosalpinx)Catches the oocyte, transports it (cilia, peristalsis); opens the peritoneal cavity to the outside
UterusFundus, body, isthmus, cervix; endometrium, myometrium, perimetriumFront: bladder; back: rectum (via pouch), sigmoid; sides: broad ligament, uterine vessels, ureter ~2 cm from the cervixImplantation, pregnancy, menstruation, labour
  • Position: usually anteverted (cervix tilted forward on the vagina) and anteflexed (body bent forward on the cervix); retroverted in ~20%.

los.text: Describe the arterial supply, and venous and lymphatic drainage of the ovary, uterus and uterine tubes
los.html:
OrganArteriesVeinsLymph
OvaryOvarian artery (aorta at L2, via the suspensory ligament)Right → IVC; left → left renal veinPara-aortic nodes
Uterine tubeOvarian + uterine (meet in the mesosalpinx)SamePara-aortic, some iliac
UterusUterine artery (internal iliac): crosses over the ureter beside the cervix, climbs tortuously in the broad ligament, joins the ovarianUterine venous plexus → internal iliac veinsFundus → para-aortic (and inguinal via round ligament); body → external iliac; cervix → internal/external iliac, sacral
  • Clinical: ovarian cancer spreads to para-aortic nodes; the ureter is at risk when the uterine artery is tied at hysterectomy.

los.text: List or identify the structures attached to the uterus
los.html:
StructureDetail
Broad ligament
  • Double fold of peritoneum from the sides of the uterus to the pelvic wall
  • Contains the tube (mesosalpinx), ovary's attachments (mesovarium), round ligament, ligament of ovary, uterine vessels, ureter at its base
Round ligamentGubernaculum remnant: uterotubal junction → deep inguinal ring → inguinal canal → labium majus; helps keep the uterus anteverted
Ligament of ovaryUterus to ovary (also gubernaculum remnant)
Uterine tubesAt the upper corners
Cervical ligaments (endopelvic fascia)Transverse cervical (cardinal), uterosacral, pubocervical
VaginaAround the cervix

los.text: Identify the levator ani and endopelvic fascia as the most important supports of the uterus (and recognise that both may be damaged during child birth)
los.html:
• Levator ani (pubococcygeus with puborectalis, iliococcygeus) + coccygeus = pelvic diaphragm: holds the viscera from below
  • Nerve to levator ani (S4) and pudendal.
Endopelvic fasciaCondensed as the cardinal, uterosacral and pubocervical ligaments, suspending the cervix and upper vagina.
Perineal body and perineal membraneSupport the lower vagina.
Childbirth
  • Stretches or tears levator ani
  • Stretches the pudendal nerve and damages fascia → uterovaginal prolapse
  • Cystocele
  • Rectocele
  • Stress incontinence (worse after menopause and with chronic straining).
Not important supportsThe round and broad ligaments.

los.text: Identify the parts of the cervix, its anatomical relationships, and name the changes that occur within the uterus during pregnancy
los.html:
Supravaginal cervixBladder in front (separated by fascia); ureters 1.5–2 cm to each side, crossed by the uterine arteries; rectouterine pouch behind.
Vaginal cervix (ectocervix)Projects into the vagina, ringed by the fornices (posterior deepest, next to the pouch of Douglas).
CanalExternal os (round in nulliparous women, slit after vaginal birth) → endocervical canal (mucus glands) → internal os.
Transformation zoneThe squamocolumnar junction where CIN and cervical cancer arise (HPV screening).
Pregnancy changeDetail
SizeMyometrium hypertrophies; fundus at the symphysis ~12 weeks, umbilicus ~20 weeks, xiphisternum ~36 weeks
Lower uterine segmentForms from the isthmus in the 3rd trimester; thin and less vascular: caesarean incision site
CervixSoftens, mucus plug; ripens, effaces and dilates in labour
Blood flowRises to ~500–750 mL/min at term
After birthInvolution over ~6 weeks

los.text: Describe the arterial supply, and venous and lymphatic drainage of the vagina
los.html:
Vagina~8–10 cm fibromuscular tube running up and back to the cervix; anterior wall shorter.
Relations
  • Front = bladder base and urethra
  • Back = rectouterine pouch (top), rectum (middle), perineal body (bottom)
  • Sides = ureters (top), levator ani.
Upper vaginaLower vagina
ArteriesVaginal artery + vaginal branches of uterine artery+ internal pudendal, middle rectal
VeinsVaginal plexus → internal iliac veinsSame
LymphInternal and external iliac nodesBelow the hymen → superficial inguinal nodes
NervesVisceral (uterovaginal plexus): stretch, little touch or painSomatic (pudendal): sensitive

los.text: Explain how the clitoris is analogous with the penis
los.html:
ClitorisPenisEmbryonic origin
Glans clitoridisGlans penisGenital tubercle
Corpora cavernosa (crura on ischiopubic rami, ischiocavernosus)Corpora cavernosaGenital tubercle
Bulbs of the vestibule (bulbospongiosus)Bulb and corpus spongiosumUrethral folds
Prepuce and frenulumPrepuce
Dorsal nerve and arteriesDorsal nerve and arteries
Difference
  • The urethra does not run through the clitoris
  • Labia minora correspond to the floor of the spongy urethra
  • Labia majora to the scrotum.
Same mechanismsErectile tissue, parasympathetic erection, pudendal sensation; testosterone/DHT decides the male pathway.

los.text: Describe the anatomy of the superficial perineal pouch
los.html:
• Location: urogenital triangle, between the perineal membrane (deep) and superficial perineal (Colles') fascia.
ContentsDetail
Erectile tissueCrura of the clitoris (under ischiocavernosus), bulbs of the vestibule (under bulbospongiosus)
MusclesIschiocavernosus, bulbospongiosus (vaginal sphincter), superficial transverse perineal (fixes the perineal body)
GlandsGreater vestibular (Bartholin's) glands
Vessels and nervesPerineal branches of the internal pudendal artery and pudendal nerve
Deep pouch(above the membrane)External urethral sphincter, compressor urethrae, deep transverse perineal; urethra and vagina pass through.
ClinicalBartholin's cysts; perineal tears involve these muscles and the perineal body.

los.text: Describe the innervation and mechanisms involved in erection of cavernous tissue
los.html:
InputNervesEffect
ParasympatheticPelvic splanchnic (S2–4) → cavernous nervesNitric oxide → cGMP → smooth muscle relaxes → clitoris and bulbs engorge; vaginal lubrication, Bartholin's secretion
SomaticPudendal (S2–4)
  • Sensation from the glans (dorsal nerve of clitoris) drives the reflex
  • Motor to ischiocavernosus and bulbospongiosus (maintain engorgement, rhythmic contractions at orgasm)
SympatheticT11–L2Smooth muscle contraction at orgasm; vasoconstriction and detumescence
